Why aren't you using the `multi_selected` signal to track the selected animation instead of this method?

this method inspects the tree itself to view selected. If we were to connect a method to the `multi_selected` signal I believe we would have to maintain another data object within `sprite_frames_editor_plugin.cpp` to track the selected state? But am open to this suggestion if theres another way

I did have a thought of changing the `animations` variable from a tree to an ItemList (similar to the frame_list). Would end up being a larger change but would also address this point since ItemList has a built in `get_selected_items` method. Thoughts on this idea?
@DexterFstone just wondering your thoughts on this - thanks!

If you ask me, I'd connect `multi_selected` and track the selected animation manually; also, there is no reason to change the animation list type to `ItemList`.
After connecting to `multi_selected`, you need to update FPS and Loop state, and you can also update the frames list to show all selected frames from all animations by selection order, so the user can watch all animations together.

It happened at `SpinBox::_update_text`, it seems the value comes from the `Range` value at line 90 in the `spin_box.cpp` file. You are changing `LineEdit` text only and not the actual value. Try `set_value_no_signal` and see if it works or not

@DexterFstone I tried updating the actual `Range` value as suggested (using `set_value_no_signal` as well when clearing out the text)- but once you click it will still show whatever the underlying range value is. I dont think there exists a way to clear/reset that value - so i wasnt able to prevent the behavior shown in your video.

Instead i implemented what i mentioned [here](https://github.com/godotengine/godot/pull/115940#issuecomment-3874462903). It will show the FPS value of the animation closest to the 0th index. This matches how frame duration handles multi select. I implemented this in my latest commit, curious your thoughts on this behavior.
